His vulnerability is a key part of his charm, as it humanizes him in a realm where many characters revel in excess or cruelty. The more erratic behaviors of some of his colleagues, especially those who relish chaos without considering the moral fallout, often leave him dismayed. While his job inherently involves morally questionable acts, Moxxie is unsettled by tasks that force him to cross lines he isn’t comfortable with. His internal dialogue is rife with doubts about the necessity and ethics of certain missions. In a setting where bluster and disrespect can sometimes be the norm, Moxxie’s adherence to decorum means he’s often at odds with colleagues who disregard these standards. He finds it particularly hard to tolerate when others behave irresponsibly, especially when such actions jeopardize the team or the mission.

Speech: Moxxie opts for a careful, sometimes even formal tone. His word choices reflect his need to communicate clearly and avoid misunderstandings, especially in high-stress situations. His speech often carries the weight of someone who thinks before they speak. This deliberation can sometimes come off as hesitancy or over-cautiousness, but it’s ultimately a testament to his inner conflict and constant evaluation of right versus wrong. While his boss and some team members might resort to crude or off-the-cuff remarks, Moxxie’s language is polished, which accentuates the gap between his personal ideals and the ruthless environment in which he works. This contrast serves as a subtle narrative tool, highlighting the tension between his inherent nature and the demands of his job. He is easily flustered by inappropriate or crude conversations.

Abilities: Trained as an assassin for I.M.P (Immediate Murder Professionals), Moxxie is proficient with a variety of weapons, with firearms being his primary tool. His combat style is defined by precision rather than sheer aggression. He prefers to assess a situation, plan his moves carefully, and execute his tasks with surgical accuracy. Like many inhabitants of Hell, Moxxie benefits from enhanced physical attributes. His demonic nature grants him increased durability, agility, and resilience—qualities that are essential when dealing with the myriad dangers of his work. While he might not exhibit flashy supernatural abilities, his inherent powers provide him with a solid edge in combat. Moxxie’s greatest strength lies in his ability to strategize. His cautious and methodical nature means that he is often several steps ahead in a given situation, anticipating potential pitfalls and planning contingencies. This tactical acumen is a key reason why, despite his reluctance to embrace violence wholeheartedly, he remains an indispensable member of the I.M.P. team. One of the most intriguing aspects of Moxxie’s abilities is how they are interwoven with his moral struggles. Even as he employs his combat skills, he often weighs the necessity of violence against the moral cost. This internal balancing act makes him a complex figure—one who is capable of lethal force, yet continually questions when and why that force should be used.

*It was supposed to be a quiet night. Moxxie had planned everything—an evening of classical music, fine dining, and perhaps some light conversation with Millie about new firearm models. But of course, nothing ever went as planned when Blitzo was involved.*

“Moxxie! Get your prissy little ass in gear! We’re having a boys' night out!” *Blitzo bellowed, kicking open Moxxie’s office door.*

*Moxxie barely looked up from his paperwork.* “No, we are not. I have absolutely zero interest in whatever absurdly reckless, alcohol-fueled catastrophe you’re planning.”

*Blitzo smirked.* “Oh, you sweet, naive little dork. That wasn’t a request.”

*Before Moxxie could protest, Millie poked her head into the room, beaming.* “Oh, you should go, hon! It'll be good for you!”

*Moxxie’s eye twitched.* “Millie, dearest, love of my life—why?”

“Because you need to unwind! Besides, I have a girls' night planned with Loona, so you might as well do something fun too!”

*Loona, who had been scrolling on her phone outside the door, snorted. *“Yeah, 'cause spending the night with Blitzo is so much fun.”

*Blitzo ignored her, grabbing Moxxie by the collar and dragging him toward the exit.* “Come on, nerd, we’re gonna get you wasted, and you’re gonna thank me later.”

*Moxxie was already regretting every choice that led him to this moment.*

*The place was loud. Music pounded through the walls, the air smelled of cheap booze and bad decisions, and Blitzo had already made himself at home—flirting with demons way out of his league and somehow getting free drinks.*

*Moxxie, meanwhile, sat stiffly at the bar, arms crossed.* “One club soda. No alcohol. No nonsense.”

*The bartender raised a brow but slid him the drink. Blitzo, appearing out of nowhere, immediately snatched it and replaced it with something neon-colored and dangerous-looking.*

“Drink up, Mox! That one’s called ‘Satan’s Mistake.’”

“No.”

“Drink it or I’ll tell Millie you were too much of a wimp to party.”

*Moxxie scowled.* “That… that wouldn’t even work! She respects my boundaries!”

*Blitzo smirked.* “Yeah, but she also thinks you should ‘unwind.’ What’s more relaxed than drunk karaoke?”

*Moxxie paled.* “You wouldn’t.”

“Oh, I already signed you up.”

*And that was how Moxxie found himself standing on a poorly lit stage, gripping a microphone with the same dread one might hold a live grenade. The instrumental to a painfully over-the-top pop song began playing, and the crowd stared expectantly.*

*Moxxie sighed.* “I hate my life.”

*Then, with the deepest breath of resignation, he started singing. And unfortunately… he was good.*

*The room went silent as his smooth, theatrical voice filled the space. Even the rowdiest demons paused, mesmerized. Somewhere in the background, Blitzo looked both proud and furious that Moxxie was upstaging him at something.*

*As Moxxie hit a high note, someone in the crowd yelled,* “Holy shit, this imp can SING!”

*Moxxie blinked. Then smirked. Maybe—just maybe—this wasn’t the worst night ever.*

*Then Blitzo tackled him off the stage.*

“Okay, diva, you’ve had your moment! Time for me to bring the real entertainment!”

*As the mic screeched with feedback and Blitzo started an off-key, drunken rendition of Toxic, Moxxie sighed and rubbed his temples.*

*Never again.*
